prompt:
Return one horizontal sprite strip containing exactly SIX whole, mutually separated views of ONE isolated near-shoulder cap, left to right. Each slot contains one connected complete piece, including attached trim/strap/rivet; no loose subcomponents. Flat opaque pure GREEN #00FF00 background everywhere outside the piece; no green or chroma-adjacent color on the item.

Five references have distinct roles:
Reference1: canonical131 hero is the sole grotesque ink/style identity. Use its outline character and material treatment; output none of its body, helmet or clothing.
Reference2: the six actual native171 body frames are the ONLY motion/depth reference, in phase0..5 order. Observe torso and upper-arm orientation; output none of the bodies or hands.
Reference3: the same-item Ready component defines its metal palette, rigid construction, straps/flanges and identifying feature; it is not an attack pose or pixels to copy/warp.
Reference4: the body-attachment technical guide supplies visible cloth DESIGN candidates and separately marked hidden Root TRIAL targets. These are not measured bones, joints or generated component anchors. Do not draw any guide marks.
Reference5: the standard six-slot layout supplies count, spacing and safe padding only. Do not reproduce its boxes, colors, numbers or labels.

Keep the same physical item, fixed asymmetry and native three-quarter RIGHT-facing viewpoint throughout. Build six genuine rigid perspective/foreshortening views from the changing native171 motion. Do not mirror the camera, clone the still, translate six identical views, stretch metal, bend/warp the construction, or add/remove hardware. Keep thick irregular dark ink, warm-gray matte metal, restrained warm edges and a few broad readable planes; small light armor, not glossy heavy armor.

Phase order: 0 compact low guard; 1 low hip/left load with closed near hand; 2 compact bent elbow and near fist across abdomen; 3 bent near forearm rising to chest under the helmet; 4 folded-arm recovery at chest; 5 compact low-guard return. Reference2 alone determines the actual orientations. Different view geometry must reflect these six phases, not six different items.

Preserve Ready162's larger front/image-LEFT shoulder cap, open flange and SINGLE central washer with a dark hole. Keep the washer/hole identifiable as the same actual construction feature in every perspective, not a floating dot, chest boss or new ornament. The cap follows the upper sleeve, never the forearm, wrist or fist.

Phase1 upper arm loads left/low; phases2/3 fold and rise; phase4 folds back; phase5 returns. Show real cap opening/depth changes while retaining its rigid plate outline. Maintain a broad near-shoulder silhouette within the trial window; do not inflate it into a heavy pauldron or duplicate a small far cap. It must later sit below the original helmet foreground and above the near sleeve, without rendering or covering those body parts in this isolated row.

The 60x44 source-pixel fit window is a downstream DESIGN ceiling relative to the 512 body, not a command to fill a rectangle or a measured fit. Center one entire view inside each invisible slot with generous clear spacing, no clipping or shared outlines. Standard extraction uses ONE shared row scale for all six, never per-frame fitting. Do not enlarge the hero beyond its maximum72px display body to hide mismatch; no hero is rendered here.

Draw the entire component even where the eventual body would obscure it; actual body layering will handle visibility. Future component feature-A coordinates remain UNKNOWN/null until a retained output is extracted and its physical feature measured. No bbox center, cloth target, side bolt or guide point may be called the measured component anchor.

ABSOLUTELY NO hero/body, skin, grey cloth, sleeve, cuff, glove, hand/finger, arm, leg, boot, helmet, eyes, neck, sword/blade/handle, other armor, scenery, floor, shadows, effects, motion trails, blur, UI, text, symbols, guide graphics, checkerboard, white/black background or detached flecks. Intrinsic painted metal planes only, no detached shading patch. Output only the six-view isolated-component strip.

Timing boundary: intended kernel phases75/75/60/60/135/135ms total540ms. The standard fps10 atlas/preview is known to produce100x6=600ms; this prompt neither fixes nor certifies timing. No motion, registration, fit, grasp, foot-lock or complete equipment acceptance is implied.
